Alamar Biosciences.why: its precision-proteomics platform (ARGO HT instruments plus NULISA multiplex panel consumables) produces the large-cohort protein datasets used for biomarker discovery and AI-based disease classification; revenue grows with instrument placements and consumable pull-through
Alamar Biosciences.evidence: Alamar Biosciences Q2 FY2026 call (08-10-2026): CFO - Q2 revenue $29.4 million, up 82%, reflecting 'rapid and broad-based adoption of our ARGO HT platform'; consumables $15.5 million, up 147%. CEO - expanded ADDI / Gates Ventures partnership adds profiling of 86,000 plasma samples with the NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel; combined data set of more than 140,000 samples made available to the global research community

players.product: NULISA precision-proteomics assays and ARGO HT System

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 total revenue was $29.4 million, up 82% from $16.2 million in Q2 2025, which the CFO attributed to rapid and broad-based adoption of the ARGO HT platform across customer segments and geographies. Consumables revenue was $15.5 million, up 147% and 53% of total revenue, on strong demand for multiplex panel kits as the installed base scaled; instrument revenue was $7.8 million, up 35%, on growth in new instrument placements; service and other revenue was $6.2 million, up 49%, mostly Technology Access Program (TAP) revenue driven by larger custom assay development projects. Gross profit was $17.7 million versus $8.6 million, and gross margin reached 60% for the first time (53% a year earlier), driven by manufacturing efficiencies as consumable production scaled and a mix shift toward higher-margin consumables.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $29.4 million (+82%); consumables $15.5 million (+147%); instruments $7.8 million (+35%); service and other $6.2 million (+49%); gross margin 60%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO guided full-year 2026 revenue to $116 million to $120 million, expected annual growth of 59% at the midpoint, and Q3 revenue to a modest sequential increase from Q2, which he defined as low single-digit sequential growth. After reaching 60%, gross margin is expected to fluctuate in the mid- to high-50s in the near term and to trend upward over time as consumables become a larger share of revenue. The company will keep investing in commercial and R&D headcount and public-company costs while staying on a 'disciplined path towards profitability'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $116 million to $120 million (59% growth at midpoint); Q3 low single-digit sequential growth; gross margin mid- to high-50s near term

quarterly_data.signal: CEO's three goals for 2026: grow the installed base by at least 100 instruments for the full year, keep per-instrument pull-through above $400,000 (which she called industry-leading), and advance into additional large cohort studies, particularly in translational and biopharma settings. CFO: installed base and average pull-through are reported annually (next on the year-end 2026 call) because new placements pressure pull-through in the near term and quarterly pull-through fluctuates; the theoretical ceiling is $5 million to $6 million per instrument at 3 plates per 24-hour period, 5 days a week. CEO: many pharma customers prefer buying more instruments for faster time to result over fully using an instrument's capacity. Year to date the majority of instrument placements went to new customers, while existing customers are adding instruments, some at additional sites.
quarterly_data.figure: at least 100 instruments added in 2026; pull-through above $400,000; theoretical ceiling $5 million to $6 million per instrument

quarterly_data.signal: The company is developing a clinical instrument, ARGO HT/DX, under a phased diagnostic enablement strategy: first obtain FDA marketing authorization for the platform, which management believes will drive use in late-phase clinical trials, open the door for partners to develop laboratory directed tests and IVD tests on it and may increase research-use demand; then partner with IVD and LDT companies on differentiated tests. CEO likened the platform to the iPhone: Alamar provides the hardware and operating system and partners build the diagnostic tests and, where applicable, seek regulatory marketing authorization. 2027 milestones: submit the ARGO HT/DX for FDA marketing authorization, launch a multiplex panel targeting a new disease area, keep growing the installed base and establish partnerships for the clinical and diagnostic enablement strategy.
quarterly_data.figure: ARGO HT/DX FDA marketing authorization submission planned for 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Content launches (CEO: 3 new RUO products launched): the Neuro 220 Panel launched in mid-March with what the CEO called incredible adoption; in early July the company launched what it calls the first commercial multiplex blood-based immunoassay for eMTBR-tau, a blood-based measurement of tau tangle burden with attomolar sensitivity, validated across multiple cohorts; about two weeks before the call it launched the NULISAseq Immune 340 Panel (approximately 340 immune-related proteins from a single blood sample, expanding on the Inflammation Panel 250), with early signs of adoption; and it launched the NULISA Dried Blood Spot Extraction Kit, making home-collected fingerstick samples compatible with the platform. Product roadmap: new content for cardiovascular and metabolic disease and oncology. The precision proteomics platform launched in January 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: Neuro 220 Panel (mid-March); eMTBR-tau assay (early July); Immune 340 Panel (approximately 340 proteins); 3 new RUO products

quarterly_data.signal: The company announced an expansion of its strategic partnership with the Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative and Gates Ventures, adding profiling of an additional 86,000 plasma samples with the NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel, building on a June 2025 multicenter initiative that profiled over 55,000 samples. It includes a national-scale initiative co-led by researchers at 3 leading universities to profile approximately 21,000 plasma samples from 10,000 Alzheimer's disease research center participants across the United States. Expected to complete in 2027, the combined data set will cover more than 140,000 samples, made available to the global research community through the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium. President: these large cohort projects have long lead times and are spread over multiple quarters; the 2026 numbers are contemplated in guidance and the rest phases in over the first half of next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 86,000 additional samples; approximately 21,000 samples in the national-scale initiative; combined data set more than 140,000 samples (completion expected 2027)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue by region: Americas 69%, EMEA 22%, APAC 9%; the company is building its international presence through distribution partnerships and direct commercial efforts. By customer: academic and research institutions 52%, biopharmaceutical companies 42%, distributors 6%. CEO: strong growth in both the academic and biopharma segments, with exceptional adoption of the neuro content; CFO: biopharma customers tend to run larger, more sustained cohort studies that drive consumables pull-through. Q4 2025 included two particularly large cohort-study orders; this year larger cohort studies are spread over many quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: Americas 69%, EMEA 22%, APAC 9%; academic 52%, biopharma 42%, distributors 6%

quarterly_data.signal: TAP serves new-customer acquisition, custom assay development and beta testing of new products and is not intended to be a long-term service business; customers are meant to buy their own instrument or transfer their work to a CRO. The Q2 TAP increase was significantly above what management had anticipated, driven by custom assay development, which the CEO reads as customers moving from discovery toward translation and clinical application. CFO expects the higher TAP volume to continue into Q3 but not at the Q2 level, and TAP services to grow at a slower rate than other areas of the business; a large portion of the installed base is still under the 1-year warranty, so maintenance contracts are a smaller part of service revenue.

Q2 2026 total operating expenses were $31.2 million versus $16.5 million: R&D $13.8 million, up 55% (higher lab supply costs for the expanding consumable panel menu and personnel), and SG&A $17.4 million, up 129% (personnel and professional services). Loss from operations was $13.5 million, including $3.3 million of stock-based compensation, and net loss was $13.2 million versus $7 million. Cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and restricted cash were $256.3 million as of June 30, 2026. CFO's capital allocation priorities: expand the commercial organization to drive instrument placements and deepen penetration of existing accounts; scale manufacturing capacity, including expanding the Fremont facility; and invest in R&D for new panels, new instruments including the ARGO HT/DX, and new applications across disease areas.
quarterly_data.figure: operating expenses $31.2 million; loss from operations $13.5 million; net loss $13.2 million; cash $256.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the research market Alamar serves today is estimated to reach $9 billion over the next decade, and the platform has the potential to expand into clinical diagnostics and population-scale early detection and health monitoring. Adoption indicators: more than 40 new publications and preprints in Q2 for a cumulative 165, and more than 140 posters and presentations featuring NULISA technology at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference, a fourfold increase year over year. CEO's read of the conference: blood-based biomarkers are going mainstream, tau is emerging as a central drug target (Biogen is advancing its tau-lowering drug into Phase III), and co-pathology is driving demand for deeply multiplexed multi-target panels.
quarterly_data.figure: research market $9 billion over the next decade; 165 cumulative publications and preprints; more than 140 posters and presentations
